clues: This is the largest city in a wide desert in the south of Israel. Dry sands stretch round it on all sides for miles and miles.
Rain here falls almost all in winter, and summers stay hot and dry. Snow is so rare that one fall in 2015 was the first since 2000.
The new city was set up at the start of the 1900s by Ottoman rulers. An old Bible town site lies just a few miles away.
Chess is huge here, thanks to skilled new folks from the old Soviet lands. No city on Earth has more top chess champs per head.
A big school for higher study, named for a past prime leader, stands in this desert city. Young folks come from all over the land to learn here.
